# Ex-FBI officials charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden laptop probe

According to prosecutors, the Foreign Influence Task Force members’ false testimony to the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 prevented lawmakers from investigating further.

Ryan Knappenberger
/ October 23, 2026

Link copied

FILE - Deputy Assistant Director for Counterterrorism at the FBI Nikki Floris, testifies before the House Judiciary Committee hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington, Oct. 22, 2019. (AP Photo/Susan Walsh, File)

WASHINGTON (CN) — The Justice Department charged two former FBI officials with lying to Congress Friday over their involvement in tax and money-laundering investigations into Hunter Biden in 2023.

Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former members of the now-disbanded Foreign Influence Task Force, were charged with making false statements to the House Judiciary Committee and surrendered to authorities.

If convicted, Floris and Benavides face up to eight years in prison.a

The case focuses on the FBI’s investigation into Hunter Biden’s laptop, acquired by the FBI on Dec. 9, 2019, which sparked conservative conspiracy theories that Joe Biden pressured Ukrainian officials while he was vice president to drop a corruption investigation into his son.

Floris served as deputy assistant director and functional head of the Foreign Influence Task Force from 2019-2022. Benavides was section chief from 2019 through the 2020 election. The Trump administration disbanded the task force in 2025.

The charges stem from a 2023 hearing before the House Judiciary Committee, where Floris and Benavides testified the task force was not involved in the FBI’s investigations into Biden. According to the DOJ, Floris told the committee she was not involved in any discussions about Biden as task force leader, while Benavides said he learned the FBI obtained Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia.

The Justice Department brought a criminal complaint against the two, a sign prosecutors have yet to present the case before a grand jury for an indictment. Grand juries in Washington have repeatedly rejected felony charges sought by the government in high-profile cases under the Trump administration.

In an initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui, Floris’ attorneys, Margaret Donovan and Mary Dohrmann, noted a criminal complaint is normally used if a defendant presents a flight risk or a danger to the community.

Faruqui noted it is uncommon for charges stemming from conduct nearly seven years ago to be brought via complaint rather than indictment. He scheduled a preliminary hearing for Tuesday.

The government claims in its affidavit that Floris and Benavides were “at the center” of the task force’s interactions with the FBI teams leading the probe into Biden. Prosecutors assert the two were tied to a 2019 analysis project referred to as “Round River,” which focused on the potential for Russian disinformation in the Hunter Biden probe.

The administration says Floris testified before the House Judiciary Committee on July 19, 2023, that she only had a “high-level” understanding of the probes and no involvement.

Benavides appeared before the committee on Sept. 28, 2023, according to prosecutors, when he similarly testified he had no knowledge of an investigation during his time on the task force.

WASHINGTON (AP) — Two former FBI officials were charged with lying to Congress about their involvement in investigating Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election, the latest in a series of splashy and politically charged actions the Justice Department has undertaken ahead of next month's midterm contests.

Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former leaders of a since-disbanded task force set up to counter foreign election interference, appeared in federal court Friday in Washington, where their lawyers pressed for a speedy hearing to contest allegations their clients lied to lawmakers by saying that they did not participate in FBI investigations of Biden.

The prosecution, a rare Department of Justice criminal case against a former employee, revisits a tangled and peculiar saga that roiled the final weeks of the 2020 race. It also comes amid a broader, backward-looking effort by FBI Director Kash Patel, who before taking over the nation’s premier law enforcement agency was a harsh critic of it, to scrutinize high-profile episodes from the bureau’s recent past that for years have animated President Donald Trump’s conservative base.

Floris’ attorneys called her “a patriot” and said she has “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years.”

“Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts,” her attorneys said in a statement. “It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”

Attorneys for Benavides accused the government of bringing “baseless criminal charges against him in a transparently political complaint.”

“This is another sad day for the Department of Justice,” his lawyers said in an emailed statement. “But now we are in court, and the truth will come out: Brad Benavides is a true patriot who devoted his career to protecting this country and its people. These charges are a disgrace.”

## A criminal complaint comes just before the midterms

The case was filed less than two weeks before the Nov. 3 elections via criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have not yet presented the allegations to a grand jury for an indictment. The Justice Department has repeatedly struggled in high-profile cases to convince grand juries in the nation’s capital to return indictments.

During the former FBI employees’ court appearance, both defense attorneys and the judge noted the unusual move to charge the case through a complaint, which is more often used by prosecutors when they have an urgent need to take people into custody because, for example, they present a danger or a risk of flight.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui remarked that it is “rare that we have charges this old coming in this nature," and over the objections of prosecutors who pushed for more time, set a preliminary hearing for next Tuesday, citing what he said was the “sword of Damocles” hanging over the defendants’ heads.

## The laptop discovery created turmoil in 2020 election

The revelation of the laptop’s existence in October 2020 injected a thorny storyline in the race between Trump, the Republican incumbent, and Biden’s father, Joe Biden, Trump’s Democratic challenger who went on to win the race.

# DOJ blocks FBI agent's Hill testimony on alleged suppression of Hunter Biden laptop story, report

The agent Elvis Chan has reportedly voluntarily agreed to appear before the committee and testify, according to the Daily Mail.

By
Charlotte Hazard

Published: September 15, 2023 2:44pm

Updated: September 15, 2023 2:46pm

* Article
* Dig Deeper

An FBI agent who allegedly lied about Big Tech being involved in the suppression of the Hunter Biden laptop story was blocked by the Justice Department from giving congressional testimony Friday, according to a news report.

The agent, Elvis Chan, has reportedly voluntarily agreed to appear before the House Judiciary Committee, represented by his personal counsel, and to testify, according to the Daily Mail.

Agency witnesses are allowed only to bring either agency counsel or personal counsel to committee interviews. They reportedly cannot bring both because the rule allows agency witnesses to be more candid in testimony with no fear of professional retribution.

Sources told the the Daily Mail the department halted the testimony because agency counsel also showed up Friday morning before the committee. Due to that circumstance, Chan's scheduled interview did not take place.

According to the outlet, an official subpoena is expected to be issued to Chan to appear for an interview next week on Sept. 21.

Chan has testified in lawsuits against the federal government in the past regarding censorship and Big Tech collusion.
